package_info.package_versions: All versions of affected NetBeans projects (26+ repositories, specific versions not listed)
package_info.why_malicious: The Octopus Scanner malware infects NetBeans project repositories, injecting malicious code into the build process so that every JAR artifact produced is backdoored. This allows the malware to propagate through the software supply chain, infecting downstream users and enabling further compromise.

execution_context.file_location: NetBeans project files (build scripts, project configuration)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During the build process, the code injects a malware payload into every newly built JAR file, ensuring that any distributed artifact is backdoored.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying build artifacts to include hidden code is a classic supply chain attack, especially when the injected code is not part of the legitimate project.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal build scripts should only package the intended application code, not inject additional, hidden payloads.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Build scripts may add legitimate instrumentation or telemetry, but this is always documented and opt-in.
key_indicators: Modification of JAR files during build
Injection of code not present in project source
No user notification or documentation of injected payload

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injected code scans the local filesystem for other NetBeans projects, infects them with the malware payload, and exfiltrates environment information to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-propagation and exfiltration of environment data are hallmarks of malware, not legitimate application behavior.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal JAR files should not scan for other projects or attempt to modify them, nor should they exfiltrate environment data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated build tools may scan for projects, but never for the purpose of infection or data exfiltration.
key_indicators: Network communication to unknown remote servers

attack_chain.action: Malware is injected into NetBeans project build scripts or configuration files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Infected JAR files are produced during the build process.

attack_chain.action: Infected JAR files are distributed to downstream users or included in other projects.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code executes when JAR is run.

attack_chain.action: Injected code executes at runtime, scanning for other NetBeans projects and infecting them.
attack_chain.leads_to: Further propagation of the malware within the developer's environment.

attack_chain.action: Malware exfiltrates environment information to a remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive data and can further compromise the environment.

behavioral_signatures: Build scripts or plugins that modify JAR files to inject additional class files or resources
JAR files containing unexpected or undocumented classes
Runtime behavior that scans for IDE project files and modifies them
Unexpected outbound network connections from build artifacts
file_indicators: NetBeans project files with modified build scripts
JAR files with injected classes not present in source
Presence of duplicate or suspicious class files in build output
network_indicators: Outbound connections to attacker-controlled domains or IPs during or after build
Exfiltration of environment variables or project metadata
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor build pipelines for unexpected modifications to JAR files, scan artifacts for undocumented or suspicious classes, and analyze network traffic from build and runtime environments for connections to unknown endpoints. Use binary fingerprinting to detect partial matches or changes in expected artifact content.
